readings.title: Yiphtaḥ's Vow and Victory
readings.subtitle: A Tragic Promise Kept
readings.text: [Judges 11:29] And the Spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came upon Yiphtaḥ, and he passed through <dn>את</dn> Gil‛ad and Menasheh, and passed through <dn>את</dn> Mitspeh of Gil‛ad. And from Mitspeh of Gil‛ad he went on toward the children of Ammon. [30] And Yiphtaḥ made a vow to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and said, “If <dn>You</dn> give <dn>את</dn> the children of Ammon into my hand, [31] then it shall be that whatever comes out of the doors of my house to meet me, when I return in peace from the children of Ammon, shall belong to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and I shall offer it up as a burnt offering.” [32] And Yiphtaḥ moved on toward the children of Ammon to fight against them, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave <dn>את</dn> them into his hands. [33] And he smote <dn>את</dn> them from Aro‛er as far as Minnith, twenty cities, and to Abĕl Keramim, with a very great slaughter. Thus the children of Ammon were humbled before the children of Yisra’ĕl. [34] And Yiphtaḥ came to his house at Mitspeh, and saw his daughter coming out to meet him with timbrels and with dancing. And she was his only child. Besides her he had neither son nor daughter. [35] And it came to be, when he saw her, that he tore <dn>את</dn> his garments, and said, “Ah, my daughter! You have brought me very low! You are among those who trouble me! For I have opened my mouth to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and I am unable to turn back.” [36] And she said to him, “My father, if you have opened <dn>את</dn> your mouth to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, do to me as has gone out of your mouth, because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has taken vengeance for you on your enemies, on the children of Ammon.” [37] And she said to her father, “Let this deed be done for me: Let me alone for two months, and let me go and wander on the mountains and bewail my maidenhood, my female friends and I.” [38] And he said, “Go.” And he sent <dn>את</dn> her away for two months. And she went with her female friends, and bewailed her maidenhood on the mountains. [39] And it came to be at the end of two months that she returned to her father, and he performed <dn>את</dn> his vow on her which he had vowed. And she knew no man. And it became a law in Yisra’ĕl, [40] that the daughters of Yisra’ĕl went yearly to lament the daughter of Yiphtaḥ the Gil‛adite four days in a year.

readings.title: Shibboleth
readings.subtitle: Conflict with Ephrayim
readings.text: [Judges 12:1] And the men of Ephrayim were summoned, and they passed over northward and said to Yiphtaḥ, “Why did you pass over to fight against the children of Ammon, and did not call us to go with you? We shall burn <dn>את</dn> your house with fire upon you.” [2] And Yiphtaḥ said to them, “My people and I were in a great struggle with the children of Ammon. And when I called you, you did not save <dn>את</dn> me out of their hands. [3] “And when I saw that you did not save <dn>את</dn> me, I put my life in my hands and passed over against the children of Ammon, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave <dn>את</dn> them into my hand. Why then have you come up to me this day to fight against me?” [4] Yiphtaḥ then gathered <dn>את</dn> all the men of Gil‛ad and fought against Ephrayim. And the men of Gil‛ad smote <dn>את</dn> Ephrayim, because they said, “You Gil‛adites are fugitives of Ephrayim among the Ephrayimites and among the Menashites.” [5] And the Gil‛adites captured <dn>את</dn> the fords of the Yardĕn before Ephrayim. And it came to be that when the fugitives of Ephrayim said, “Let me pass over,” that the men of Gil‛ad said to him, “Are you an Ephrayimite?” If he said, “No,” [6] then they would say to him, “Please say ‘Shibboleth’!” And he would say, “Sibboleth,” for he was unable to pronounce it right. Then they seized <dn>את</dn> him and slew <dn>את</dn> him at the fords of the Yardĕn. And forty-two thousand Ephrayimites fell at that time. [7] And Yiphtaḥ judged <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ĕl six years. And Yiphtaḥ the Gil‛adite died and was buried in the cities of Gil‛ad.

readings.title: Ibtsan, Ělon, and Abdon
readings.subtitle: Minor Judges of Yisra’ĕl
readings.text: [Judges 12:8] And after him Ibtsan of Bĕyth Leḥem judged <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ĕl. [9] And he had thirty sons, and gave away thirty daughters to those outside, and brought in thirty daughters from outside for his sons. And he judged <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ĕl seven years. [10] And Ibtsan died and was buried at Bĕyth Leḥem. [11] And after him Ělon the Zebulunite judged <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ĕl. And he judged <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ĕl ten years. [12] And Ělon the Zebulunite died and was buried at Ayalon in the land of Zebulun. [13] And after him Abdon son of Hillel the Pir‛athonite judged <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ĕl. [14] And he had forty sons and thirty grandsons who rode on seventy young donkeys. And he judged <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ĕl eight years. [15] And Abdon son of Hillel the Pir‛athonite died and was buried in Pir‛athon in the land of Ephrayim, in the mountains of the Amalĕqites.

readings.title: The Birth of Shimshon
readings.subtitle: The Nazirite Vow
readings.text: [Judges 13:1] And the children of Yisra’ĕl again did evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave <dn>את</dn> them into the hand of the Peleshetites forty years. [2] And there was a certain man of Tsor‛ah, of the clan of the Danites, whose name was Manoḥ, and his wife was barren and had not borne. [3] And the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> appeared to the woman and said to her, <dq>“See now, you are barren and have not borne, but you shall conceive and bear a son.</dq> [4] <dq>“And now, please be on guard, and do not drink wine or strong drink, and do not eat any unclean thing.</dq> [5] <dq>“For see, you are conceiving and bearing a son. And no razor shall come upon his head, for the child is a Nazirite to <dn>Elohim</dn> from the womb. And he shall begin to save <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ĕl out of the hand of the Peleshetites.”</dq> [6] And the woman came and spoke to her husband, saying, “A Man of <dn>Elohim</dn> came to me, and <dn>His</dn> appearance was like the appearance of a Messenger of <dn>Elohim</dn>, very awesome. And I did not ask <dn>Him</dn> where <dn>He</dn> was from, and <dn>He</dn> did not declare <dn>His</dn> Name to me. [7] “And <dn>He</dn> said to me, ‘See, you are conceiving and bearing a son. And now, drink no wine or strong drink, nor eat any unclean thing, for the child is a Nazirite to <dn>Elohim</dn> from the womb to the day of his death.’ ” [8] And Manoḥ prayed to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and said, “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, please let the Man of <dn>Elohim</dn> whom <dn>You</dn> sent come to us again, and teach us what we should do for the child who is to be born.” [9] And <dn>Elohim</dn> listened to the voice of Manoḥ, and the Messenger of <dn>Elohim</dn> came to the woman again as she was sitting in the field, but Manoḥ her husband was not with her. [10] And the woman hurried and ran and declared to her husband, and said to him, “See, the Man who came to me the other day has appeared to me!” [11] And Manoḥ rose up and followed his wife, and came to the Man and said to <dn>Him</dn>, “Are <dn>You</dn> the Man who spoke to the woman?” And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“I am.”</dq> [12] And Manoḥ said, “Now let <dn>Your</dn> words come to pass! What is the rule for the child and his work?” [13] And the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Manoḥ, <dq>“Let the woman be on guard against all that <dn>I</dn> said to her.</dq> [14] <dq>“She is not to eat of all that comes from the vine of wine, nor drink wine or strong drink, nor eat any unclean thing. All that <dn>את</dn> <dn>I</dn> commanded her she is to guard.”</dq> [15] And Manoḥ said to the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “Please let us detain <dn>את</dn> <dn>You</dn>, and prepare a young goat for <dn>You</dn>.” [16] And the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Manoḥ, <dq>“Though you detain <dn>Me</dn>, <dn>I</dn> do not eat your bread. But if you offer <dn>את</dn> a burnt offering, offer it to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”</dq> For Manoḥ did not know <dn>He</dn> was the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [17] And Manoḥ said to the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “What is <dn>Your</dn> Name, so that when <dn>Your</dn> words come to pass we shall esteem <dn>You</dn>?” [18] And the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, <dq>“Why do you ask about <dn>My</dn> Name, seeing it is wonderful?”</dq> [19] And Manoḥ took <dn>את</dn> the young goat and <dn>את</dn> the grain offering, and offered it upon the rock to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And <dn>He</dn> did a wondrous thing while Manoḥ and his wife looked on: [20] it came to be, as the flame went up toward the heavens from the altar, that the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> went up in the flame of the altar. And Manoḥ and his wife were looking on, and they fell on their faces to the ground. [21] And the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> did not appear any more to Manoḥ and his wife. Then Manoḥ knew that <dn>He</dn> was the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [22] And Manoḥ said to his wife, “We shall certainly die, because we have seen <dn>Elohim</dn>!” [23] But his wife said to him, “If <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had desired to kill us, <dn>He</dn> would not have received a burnt offering and a grain offering from our hands, nor would <dn>He</dn> have shown us <dn>את</dn> all these, nor would <dn>He</dn> have let us hear the like of this at this time.” [24] And the woman bore a son and called his name Shimshon. And the child grew, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> blessed <dn>את</dn> him. [25] And the Spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> began to move <dn>את</dn> him at Maḥaneh Dan between Tsor‛ah and Eshta’ol.

readings.title: Shimshon's Riddle
readings.subtitle: The Lion and the Honey
readings.text: [Judges 14:1] And Shimshon went down to Timnath, and saw a woman in Timnath of the daughters of the Peleshetites. [2] And he went up and declared it to his father and mother, saying, “I have seen a woman in Timnath of the daughters of the Peleshetites. And now, take <dn>את</dn> her for me as a wife.” [3] And his father and mother said to him, “Is there no woman among the daughters of your brothers, or among all my people, that you must go and get a wife from the uncircumcised Peleshetites?” And Shimshon said to his father, “Take <dn>את</dn> her for me, for she is right in my eyes.” [4] But his father and mother did not know that it was of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that <dn>He</dn> was seeking an occasion against the Peleshetites. For at that time the Peleshetites were ruling over Yisra’ĕl. [5] And Shimshon went down to Timnath with his father and mother, and they came to the vineyards of Timnath. And see, a young lion came roaring against him. [6] And the Spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came mightily upon him, and he tore <dn>את</dn> it apart as one would have torn apart a young goat, though he had nothing in his hand. But he did not declare to his father or mother what he had done. [7] And he went down and spoke to the woman, and she was right in the eyes of Shimshon. [8] And after a few days he returned to take <dn>את</dn> her, and he turned aside to see <dn>את</dn> the carcass of the lion. And see, a swarm of bees and honey were in the carcass of the lion. [9] And he took some of it in his hands, and went along, eating. And he went to his father and mother, and gave some to them, and they ate. But he did not declare to them that he had taken the honey out of the carcass of the lion. [10] And his father went down to the woman. And Shimshon made a feast there, for young men used to do so. [11] And it came to be, when they saw <dn>את</dn> him, that they brought thirty companions to be with him. [12] And Shimshon said to them, “Let me put a riddle to you. If you clearly explain <dn>את</dn> it to me within the seven days of the feast, and find it out, then I shall give you thirty linen garments and thirty changes of garments. [13] “But if you are unable to explain <dn>את</dn> it to me, then you shall give me thirty linen garments and thirty changes of garments.” And they said to him, “Put your riddle, and let us hear it.” [14] And he said to them, “Out of the eater came something to eat, and out of the strong came something sweet.” And they were unable to explain the riddle in three days. [15] And it came to be on the seventh day that they said to Shimshon’s wife, “Entice <dn>את</dn> your husband, that he might explain <dn>את</dn> the riddle to us, lest we burn <dn>את</dn> you and <dn>את</dn> your father’s house with fire. Have you invited us to take what is ours? Is it not so?” [16] And Shimshon’s wife wept on him, and said, “You only hate <dn>את</dn> me! You do not love <dn>את</dn> me! You have put a riddle to the sons of my people, but you have not explained <dn>את</dn> it to me.” And he said to her, “See, I have not explained it to my father or my mother, so should I explain it to you?” [17] And she wept on him the seven days while their feast lasted. And it came to be on the seventh day that he explained <dn>את</dn> it to her, because she pressed him. And she explained <dn>את</dn> the riddle to the sons of her people. [18] And the men of the city said to him on the seventh day before the sun went down, “What is sweeter than honey? And what is stronger than a lion?” And he said to them, “If you had not plowed with my heifer, you would not have found out my riddle!” [19] And the Spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came mightily upon him, and he went down to Ashqelon and smote thirty of their men, and took <dn>את</dn> their garments, and gave the changes of garments to those who explained the riddle. And his wrath burned, and he went up to his father’s house. [20] And Shimshon’s wife was given to his companion, who had been his friend.

readings.title: Foxes, Fire, and the Jawbone
readings.subtitle: Shimshon's Revenge
readings.text: [Judges 15:1] And it came to be after a while, in the time of wheat harvest, that Shimshon visited <dn>את</dn> his wife with a young goat. And he said, “Let me go in to my wife, into her room.” But her father would not allow him to go in. [2] And her father said, “I really thought that you hated <dn>את</dn> her intensely, so I gave <dn>את</dn> her to your companion. Is not her younger sister better than she? Please, take her instead.” [3] And Shimshon said to them, “This time I am blameless regarding the Peleshetites if I do evil to them.” [4] And Shimshon went and caught three hundred foxes, and took torches, and turned the foxes tail to tail, and put a torch between every two tails. [5] And he set the torches on fire, and let the foxes go into the standing grain of the Peleshetites, and burned up both the shocks and the standing grain, as well as the vineyards and olive groves. [6] And the Peleshetites said, “Who has done this?” And they answered, “Shimshon, the son-in-law of the Timnite, because he has taken <dn>את</dn> his wife and given <dn>את</dn> her to his companion.” And the Peleshetites came up and burned <dn>את</dn> her and <dn>את</dn> her father with fire. [7] And Shimshon said to them, “Since you would do this, I shall surely take revenge on you, and after that I cease.” [8] And he smote <dn>את</dn> them hip and thigh with a great slaughter. And he went down and dwelt in the cleft of the rock of Ěytam. [9] And the Peleshetites went up and encamped in Yehudah, and were spread out in Leḥi. [10] And the men of Yehudah said, “Why have you come up against us?” And they answered, “We have come up to arrest <dn>את</dn> Shimshon, to do to him as he has done to us.” [11] And three thousand men of Yehudah went down to the cleft of the rock of Ěytam, and said to Shimshon, “Do you not know that the Peleshetites rule over us? What is this you have done to us?” And he said to them, “As they did to me, so I have done to them.” [12] And they said to him, “We have come down to arrest <dn>את</dn> you, to give <dn>את</dn> you into the hand of the Peleshetites.” And Shimshon said to them, “Swear to me that you do not fall upon me yourselves.” [13] And they spoke to him, saying, “No, but we shall bind <dn>את</dn> you securely and give <dn>את</dn> you into their hand, but we shall certainly not put <dn>את</dn> you to death.” And they bound <dn>את</dn> him with two new ropes and brought him up from the rock. [14] He came to Leḥi, and the Peleshetites came shouting to meet him. And the Spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came mightily upon him, and the ropes that were on his arms became like flax that is burned with fire, and his bonds broke loose from his hands. [15] And he found a fresh jawbone of a donkey, and put out his hand and took it, and smote a thousand men with it. [16] And Shimshon said, “With the jawbone of a donkey, heaps upon heaps, with the jawbone of a donkey I have smitten a thousand men!” [17] And it came to be, when he had ended speaking, that he threw the jawbone from his hand, and called that place Ramath Leḥi. [18] And he became very thirsty, and cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and said, “<dn>You</dn> have given <dn>את</dn> this great deliverance by the hand of <dn>Your</dn> servant. And now, shall I die of thirst and fall into the hand of the uncircumcised?” [19] And <dn>Elohim</dn> opened <dn>את</dn> the hollow place that is in Leḥi, and water came out, and he drank. And his spirit returned and he revived. Therefore he called its name Ěn Haqqorĕ, which is in Leḥi to this day. [20] And he judged <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ĕl in the days of the Peleshetites twenty years.
